features.title: Sync backlog items with a Gitea or Forgejo repository
features.summary: Serves the backlog's backlog-provider Host API as the gitea kind: a connection (Instance URL, access token reference) names the account (or notes a token without read:user) and discovers the repositories with issues it can see through repository search; a binding to an owner/repo pulls issues changed since an updated_at checkpoint with the inclusive since= filter, every page of 50, skipping pull requests, and maps the title, the markdown body, open/closed (open stands for inbox, todo and doing; closed for done and dropped), labels as tags (missing labels created unless the binding says no) and issue dependencies as depends-on/blocks both ways; comments flow both ways; deleting a linked item closes its issue. 429 and 503 wait for Retry-After up to three times.
features.currentSurface: Backlog settings › Remote sync › Add Gitea connection (rendered by @dshfiles/backlog)

configuration.constraints: A secret:ALIAS reference to a Gitea/Forgejo access token with write:issue and write:repository, resolved on the Host; empty falls back to GITEA_TOKEN, then FORGEJO_TOKEN.

The Instance URL, the instance web root such as https://gitea.example.com (a trailing /api/v1 is accepted, a bare host reads as https); required: the connection form names the field, waits for it before Test and Save, and the Host refuses to save a connection without it; https, or plain http only for loopback, private or CGNAT addresses and .internal/.local/.lan/.home.arpa/.ts.net names.
owner/repo, or empty for the only repository with issues the token sees.
no, false, off or 0 only attaches labels that already exist in the repository.

failureModes: A refused token (401/403) fails the call with its recovery: check the key, its write:issue and write:repository scopes and the repository access; the token never appears in the message.

A missing or public plain-http Instance URL or an invalid owner/repo fails before any request with target-missing, naming what to set; the connection form keeps Test and Save disabled while the Instance URL is empty and says what to enter.
A reference on another host, a pull request or a malformed key fails with not-found before or instead of a write.
A repository with issue dependencies turned off reads no relations and syncs the other fields.
Still rate-limited after three Retry-After waits fails the call with a 429; the next pass retries from the same checkpoint.

externalDependencies.boundary: HTTP(S) requests to the connection's instance under /api/v1 with Authorization: token: user, repos/search, repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues, issues/{n}, issues/{n}/comments, issues/{n}/labels, issues/{n}/dependencies, issues/{n}/blocks and repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: src/gitea-fake.ts answers the same paths in memory through an HttpClient stand-in: repository acme/app with issues, a pull request, labels, comments and dependencies, newest-first listing, inclusive since= on whole seconds, limit capped at 50, +01:00 timestamps, a read:user scope switch, dependencies switch and 429s on demand; the provider, its retry and decoding run for real.

verification.testName: names the account and discovers repositories with issues, and still works without read:user
accepts the base URL with /api/v1, and refuses public plain http, a bad repository and a foreign reference before any request
asks for the instance URL by name, requires it, and reads a bare host as https
allows plain http only for private hosts
pulls every page whatever the order, skips pull requests, and checkpoints the newest update
writes title, body, status and labels, creating a missing label unless the binding says no
reads and writes dependencies as depends-on and blocks, and reads none when dependencies are off
creates an issue with its labels, kind and closed state, then its dependencies, in the only repository when the binding names none
reads comments with fetch and adds one
resolves numbers, owner/repo#n and issue URLs on the instance, and refuses pull requests
waits for Retry-After on a 429, then gives up after three retries
reports a refused token with its recovery and never echoes the token
answers the backlog over its Host API with the failure code intact

telemetry.testName: records one gitea request span per call, with the operation and status only
